name: Nicolas Cazzaniga
title: Ecology, Evolution and Behavior Program, City University of New York
years: Graduate student from 2022 - Ph.D. on systematics, evolution and biogeography of the Neotropical whip spider family Phrynidae
bio: Nick completed his B.S. in Entomology at Purdue University in 2019, where his capstone thesis analyzed social versus solitary growth rates in the Socotra Island Blue Baboon tarantula, *Monocentropus balfouri*. During his undergraduate tenure, he dedicated significant time to the Yale insect collection and various entomology laboratories on the Purdue campus. Nick pivoted his focus toward the understudied arachnid orders after working with live specimens in Purdue’s invertebrate zoo and within the exotic pet trade. Following a brief residency in the zoological sector at the Maritime Aquarium, he was awarded a Graduate Student Fellowship from the AMNH in 2022. He is currently conducting his doctoral research on the systematics and biogeography of the amblypygid family *Phrynidae* through the Ecology and Evolutionary Biology PhD program at the City University of New York. His work is supported by an NSF grant focused on the Systematics and Evolution of Pedipalpi.
